extracted.intended_audience: economists, empirical researchers, and policy analysts using USPTO historical patent data
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and definitions for constructing and using the USPTO Historical Patent Files and derived annual, monthly, and monthly_disposal datasets (1981–2014 coverage emphasis). For researchers analyzing application flows, disposals, pendency, and technology classification (NBER sub-categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Era definition for classes and subclasses
rubrics_metrics.description: For each class and subclass, an era begins the day of an order which modifies the class or subclass and ends the day before the subsequent order affecting that class or subclass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Classification Order 1902 (Jan 4, 2011) caused classes/subclasses it directly modified to begin a new era; eras remain constant for classes/subclasses not affected by an order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of orders_class and orders_subclass for ambiguous NBER mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Since each Classification Order does not alter the entire USPC system, the orders_class and orders_subclass data files are used to apply NBER sub-categories where matching class-at-disposal or current class to NBER sub-category yielded an ambiguous result (probability of less than 75%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If class-to-NBER assignment probability <75%, consult classification orders to resolve assignment across eras.

rubrics_metrics.name: historical_masterfile contents and key variables
rubrics_metrics.description: The historical_masterfile contains detailed data on each published or publicly-available non-published application, including appl_id, pubno, patent, nber (NBER sub-category), uspc and uspc_sub (current USPC class and subclass), ipc and cpc, appl_dt, prior_dt, pub_dt, disp_dt, disp_ty, pta, and exp_dt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These variables are aggregated into annual, monthly and monthly_disposal datasets. Use this file to generate time-series and cohort analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: exp_dt_max for 1836–1861 period
rubrics_metrics.description: The variable exp_dt_max represents the upper limit of the expiration date for the period 1836–1861, during which the Commissioner could extend a patent’s statutory term by seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because records of which patents received extensions are not available, researchers should treat exp_dt_max as an upper-bound (not definitive) expiration date for patents in this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Back-filling missing application dates (appl_dt)
rubrics_metrics.description: 39 appl_dt values missing from PALM are back-filled using the PTMT Custom Bibliographic Patent Data Extract DVD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DVD is updated only through 2013, so application dates for more recent filings may still be missing; acknowledge this limitation in analyses requiring complete appl_dt coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: annual data file composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual data file includes annual counts of granted patents and patents-in-force by NBER sub-category, and aggregated filed applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the annual file for long-run trends and decade-level analyses; patents-in-force are useful control variables for cross-time comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: monthly data file start date and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The monthly data file begins in January 1981, the first year of reliable patent application data, and captures many of the same variables as the annual file but also adds abandoned and pending application counts, by NBER category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses requiring abandoned vs pending counts should use monthly data starting 1981; earlier periods lack sufficient abandonment data to distinguish categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: monthly_disposal dataset purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The monthly_disposal data file follows prosecution outcomes over time for each monthly application filing cohort across NBER categories; it provides the distribution of disposal dates for each monthly filing cohort from 1981 to 2014, separated by disposal type (grants and abandonments) and by NBER sub-category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset is cohort-based and anonymized (no identifiers for individual applications); it is intended to analyze pendency and abandonment dynamics rather than to track individual case histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of disposals (terminal outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: For all incoming applications to the PTO, there are only two possible terminal outcomes (disposals): applications are either issued as granted patents, or they are abandoned. Applications that have yet to be disposed are pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination decisions such as allowances and rejections are not technically disposals; allowances require applicant action (fee payment) to become grants, so issuance/grant date is used as the disposal date in the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposal/issuance date convention
rubrics_metrics.description: In the data file, the day that the patent is published is used as the disposal, or issuance, date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because allowances are not final disposals until grant/issuance, use the publication/grant date when computing disposal-based statistics (e.g., allowance/issuance rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of abandonment and date back-filling
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposal through abandonment can occur either by express abandonment or automatically when an applicant fails to respond to an office action (typically within six months). When the examiner eventually files the abandonment, the abandonment date is back-filled to reflect the initial response deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This back-filling practice can produce right censoring for the most recent six or so months in the time series and must be accounted for when interpreting recent abandonment counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right censoring for recent months
rubrics_metrics.description: Because examiners may wait before officially filing an abandonment (in case of revival petitions) and because abandonment dates are back-filled, there is some degree of right censoring for the six or so most recent months in the time series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasets are constructed through Dec 31, 2014 to reduce undercounting; researchers should be cautious analyzing very recent months due to potential incomplete back-filled abandonments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion of application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Included: 'regular' utility patent applications, utility applications filed as national stage entries of a parent PCT application, and converted provisional applications. Excluded: provisional applications, re-issue applications, and PCT applications (except national stage entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that analysis of 'new filings' uses the same inclusion rules; note that some official statistics include RCEs whereas this dataset excludes them for counts of new filings and abandonments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of RCEs and continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs) are a version of 'non-serialized continuations' that retain the serial number of the parent application; because the parent and child applications are substantially the same and the parent is simultaneously abandoned, RCEs are excluded from counts of new filings and abandonments. Traditional continuations (including continuations-in-part and divisionals) are included because they do not necessitate abandonment of the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about whether your count includes RCEs when comparing to other official statistics; inclusion/exclusion materially affects counts of new filings and pending stocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock of pending applications calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The stock of pending applications at the end of the month is determined by the inflow of incoming applications and the outflow of grants and abandonments during that month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cohort-based monthly_disposal distributions to reconstruct stocks; beware of left truncation and data start-date limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left truncation and start of reliable pending stock reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Since detailed application data begin only in January 1981, there is left truncation on new applications. Using the average survival curve for 1981–1983 cohorts, only 1% of applications are still pending as of 73 months after filing. Therefore the monthly data file reports the estimated stock of pending applications beginning 73 months after January 1981 (February 1987) to minimize undercounting due to left truncation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building long-run monthly series of pending applications, begin reported pending stock no earlier than Feb 1987 (73 months after Jan 1981) to reduce bias from left truncation.

rubrics_metrics.name: monthly_disposal counts represent cumulative stocks within appl_month
rubrics_metrics.description: The counts in monthly_disposal are cumulative within each appl_month, so that they represent stocks, not flows. The number of issued, abandoned and pending applications always sum to the corresponding number of applications for that entry cohort and NBER sub-category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret monthly_disposal outputs as cohort cumulative incidence functions (CIFs) and survival curves rather than as per-month flows; to get flows, differentiate cumulative counts across months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance vs grant terminology and measurement caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Some confusion exists because grants are sometimes called 'allowances,' and the grant rate (the number of issuances divided by the number of disposals) is sometimes called the allowance rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether analyses use allowance (examiner allowance decision) or issuance/grant (publication/grant date) concept when reporting rates; the dataset uses issuance/grant date as the disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting allowance rates in dynamic contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: In a dynamic context, information about stocks and flows alone is not enough to accurately distinguish between pendency and the rate of abandonment when those may be varying over time. If abandonments generally occur faster than grants, then the ratio of granted patents to abandonments ('allowance rate') will trend downward even if quality is constant. Changes in duration of pendency also complicate comparisons across cohorts or time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should use cohort-based monthly_disposal data to disentangle timing effects from terminal rates and be cautious comparing raw allowance rates across growing cohorts or periods with changing pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data coverage end date and disposal capture objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset tracks monthly disposals for each monthly application cohort until all applications are disposed of via issuance or abandonment (unless applications remain pending as of December 31, 2014). The data file goes through the end of 2014 to ensure a sufficient period of time to capture all abandonments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses of terminal outcomes should acknowledge that the dataset's observation window ends 2014; cohorts filed near 2014 will necessarily have incomplete terminal outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBER classification algorithm performance and added codes
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBER classification algorithm successfully assigned a single NBER sub-category to a high share of applications/patents (Table 1: applications 96.91% classified; patents 99.95% classified). Sub-categories 70 (Not classified) and 80 (Missing) and consequently categories 7 and 8 were added to account for cases the algorithm couldn't label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using NBER-coded results, account for the small fraction of Not classified/Missing codes and the algorithm's probabilistic nature; consult era/order files for ambiguous assignments (<75% probability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patents-in-force as a normalization/control variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of patents-in-force may be particularly valuable control variables for multiple streams of research (e.g., to indicate how crowded technology spaces are over time). Normalizing by patents-in-force (e.g., applications per patent-in-force) helps compare growth rates across time and technology spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include patents-in-force as controls in cross-time analyses (litigation rates, application intensity) to account for changes in the stock of extant patents that could affect denominators and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Gini coefficient to measure concentration across classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gini coefficient can be generalized to examine the distribution of patents across classes; we calculated Gini over time for classification schemes (USPC class/subclass and NBER sub-category) to assess concentration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers can adopt the Gini metric to quantify concentration and track changes in technological concentration over time; be mindful that reclassification orders may affect observed trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: monthly_disposal intended research uses
rubrics_metrics.description: The monthly_disposal data file is intended to provide more information about pendency and abandonment for researchers; it provides, for the first time, detailed information about disposal and pendency for patent applications across NBER categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monthly_disposal to analyze timing of disposals (survival curves and cumulative incidence of grants vs abandonments) and to compare terminal rates across cohorts and technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulating the dataset for exit cohort analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the dataset tracks entry cohorts, it could be manipulated to capture exit cohorts for more in-depth analysis of exit pendency or allowance rate by exit cohort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers interested in exit-cohort perspectives should re-index cohort definitions using disposal dates and map back to entry cohorts as necessary; methodology references (e.g., Mitra-Kahn et al.) are provided for cohort techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' decisions are not guaranteed terminal outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination decisions by examiners (allowances and rejections) are not technically disposals; applicants may respond (e.g., appeals to PTAB or to federal courts), so rejections do not necessarily represent terminal disposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses of terminal outcomes should treat examiner actions as intermediate events; only recorded issuance/grant and abandonment are terminal in the dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical notes on express abandonment frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Express abandonment is fairly rare. Internal statistics show express abandonments peaked in 2002 at 7.6% (as a proportion of all abandonments) and fell to 2.1% in 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect most abandonments to be failures to respond rather than express abandonments; this affects interpretation of abandonment timing and back-filling practices.
